court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court, Villupuram in HMOP.No.48 of 2019

parties.respondent_defendant: Rekha and Ramesh (wife and her paramour)

facts_of_case: Marriage between Manikandan and Rekha was solemnized on 24.01.2011. Rekha did not perform her moral obligations and there were frequent quarrels between the parties. The petitioner had earlier given a complaint before the All Women Police Station at Villupuram in the year 2015 with respect to non-performance of marital duties.

legal_principles.principle: Production of a photograph is not sufficient to prove the allegation of adultery.
legal_principles.held: It had been observed that production of a photograph would not be sufficient to prove the allegation of adultery.

legal_principles.principle: It is a very difficult task to prove the allegations of adultery since the physical relationship between the parties has to be established.
legal_principles.held: However, it had been further observed that it is a very difficult task to prove the allegations of adultery since the physical relationship between the parties had to be established.

legal_principles.principle: Circumstantial evidence can be used to prove the allegations of adultery.
legal_principles.held: The learned counsel would place reliance on the evidence of PW3 and PW4 and particularly on the evidence of PW4, who had also taken a photograph of the first and second respondent, sitting together in close proximity and talking with each other.

outcome.final_order: The judgment and decree passed by the Family Court, Villupuram in HMOP.No.48 of 2019 dated 01.08.2022 is set-aside.
